wikipedia#0.title: 2019: President Martín Vizcarra dissolved the Congress of Peru, resulting in a constitutional crisis.

wikipedia#1.title: 2009: A 7.6 MW earthquake struck off the southern coast of Sumatra, Indonesia (damage pictured), killing 1,115 and impacting an estimated 1.2 million people.

wikipedia#2.title: 2005: The Danish newspaper Jyllands-Posten published controversial editorial cartoons depicting Muhammad, sparking protests across the Islamic world by many who viewed them as Islamophobic and blasphemous.

wikipedia#3.title: 2000: Twelve-year-old Muhammad al-Durrah was shot dead in the Gaza Strip; the Israel Defense Forces initially accepted responsibility but retracted it five years later.

wikipedia#4.title: 1998: The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), a nonprofit organization that manages the assignment of domain names and IP addresses in the Internet, was incorporated.

wikipedia#5.title: 1982: Cheers, an American television sitcom, debuted with its pilot episode on NBC.

wikipedia#6.title: 1975: The Boeing AH-64 Apache (example pictured), the primary attack helicopter for a number of countries, made its first flight.

wikipedia#7.title: 1955: American film actor James Dean suffered fatal injuries in a head-on car accident near Cholame, California.

wikipedia#8.title: 1939: NBC broadcast the first televised American football game, between the Fordham Rams and the Waynesburg Yellow Jackets.

wikipedia#9.title: 1939: Second World War: General Władysław Sikorski (pictured) became the first prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile.

wikipedia#10.title: 1938: Adolf Hitler, Benito Mussolini, Neville Chamberlain, and Édouard Daladier signed the Munich Agreement, stipulating that Czechoslovakia must cede the Sudetenland to Germany.

wikipedia#11.title: 1920: Times Square Theater (pictured) opened on Broadway with a production of The Mirage, a play written by its owner, Edgar Selwyn.

wikipedia#12.title: 1918: Nestor Makhno and Fedir Shchus led insurgents to successfully ambush the Central Powers that occupied southern Ukraine during World War I.

wikipedia#13.title: 1882: The Vulcan Street Plant in Appleton, Wisconsin, the first hydroelectric central station to serve a system of private and commercial customers in North America, went online.

wikipedia#14.title: 1863: Georges Bizet's opera Les pêcheurs de perles premiered at the Théâtre Lyrique in Paris.

wikipedia#15.title: 1791: Mozart conducted the premiere of his last opera, The Magic Flute, in Vienna.

wikipedia#16.title: 1551: Sue Takafusa, a retainer of the Ōuchi clan in western Japan, led a coup against the daimyō Ōuchi Yoshitaka, leading to the latter's forced suicide.

wikipedia#17.title: 1342: An Anglo-Breton army defeated a far larger Franco-Breton force in the first land battle of the Hundred Years' War.

wikipedia#18.title: 1139: A violent earthquake struck the Caucasus near Ganja, killing up to an estimated 300,000 people.

wikipedia#19.title: 737: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana: Türgesh tribesmen attacked and captured the exposed baggage train of the Umayyad army, sent ahead of the main force.
